The figure presents a block diagram illustrating the proposed system architecture for agitation detection using data from an E4 wristband. The overall layout is structured as a two-row flowchart, with the top row representing the initial data processing pipeline and the bottom row depicting the core learning and detection modules. The diagram flows from left to right, with directional arrows indicating the sequence of operations.

In the top row, the first module is labeled 'E4 Wristband Data', represented as a rounded rectangle with a dashed border, light gray fill, and black text. This module serves as the input source. It connects via a solid gray arrow to the next module, 'Data Pre-Processing', which has identical visual attributes. Following this, another arrow leads to 'Feature Extraction', also styled consistently with the previous blocks. From 'Feature Extraction', a horizontal line extends to the right and then bends downward to connect to the first module in the bottom row.

The bottom row begins with 'Variational Autoencoder', again depicted as a rounded rectangle with a dashed border, light gray background, and black text. This module receives input from 'Feature Extraction' via the connecting line described above. An arrow proceeds from 'Variational Autoencoder' to 'Self-Training Learning', which maintains the same visual style. Finally, an arrow leads from 'Self-Training Learning' to 'Agitation Detection', the last module in the sequence, styled identically to all others.

All connections are represented by solid gray arrows with pointed heads, indicating unidirectional data flow. There are no feedback loops or bidirectional connections shown. The diagram uses consistent visual attributes across all modules: rounded rectangular shapes with dashed borders, light gray fills, subtle drop shadows, and centered black text. The entire structure is clean and minimalistic, emphasizing the sequential nature of the pipeline from raw sensor data to final agitation detection output.
